name: Port Alder
blurb: A small Michigan lake town in the last good weeks of boating season: a garage that needs you, a loan and a landlord to keep paid, a friend with a pontoon, and a harbor festival on the way.
contentNotes: All-ages. Everyday money, work and friendship. No real people, businesses or events; Port Alder is fictional and the numbers are approximate 2025-26 US figures.

realism.rationale: Simulation shows off everything the engine can count: payroll with withholding, rent and loan payments, a credit card with statements, fuel and maintenance, and the weekly lives of the people around you. Drop it to Grounded or Story for a lighter chat.

currency.label: US dollars
currency.note: Money is integer cents. National prices are scaled by the region's cost-of-living multiplier (Michigan 0.95) at pricing time.

start.summary: Your alarm has gone off over the hardware store on Harbor Street. It is gray and cool, the lake is flat, and the garage opens at seven with a list of cars waiting.

places.name: Lakeshore County
places.description: A long strip of dunes, orchards and small harbor towns on the east shore of Lake Michigan.

places.name: Port Alder
places.description: A harbor town of about 6,500 people with a brick Main Street, a working marina, two stoplights and an unreasonable number of coffee shops in summer.

places.name: 114 Harbor Street
places.description: A three-storey brick building with Harbor Hardware on the ground floor and four apartments above. Unit 2B has a lake view if you lean out of the bathroom window.

places.name: Alder Automotive
places.description: A three-bay repair shop on Lake Avenue with a customer counter, a parts shelf and a back lot full of cars waiting for one more part. The radio is always on.

places.name: The Rusty Anchor
places.description: A waterfront bar and grill with a deck over the harbor, a wall of old buoys and the best burger in the county. Trivia is on Thursdays.

places.name: Bluebird Coffee
places.description: A bright corner cafe on Main Street with mismatched chairs, a good espresso machine and a pastry case that empties by ten.

places.name: Alder Township Hall
places.description: A low brick building with a flagpole and a bulletin board. Permits, tax bills and the township's vehicle yard are all handled here.

places.name: Alder Community Clinic
places.description: A one-storey clinic with urgent care, a pharmacy window and a waiting room that smells of hand sanitizer and old magazines.

places.name: Alder Harbor Marina
places.description: Eighty slips, a boat ramp, a fuel dock and a barn full of winter storage. The harbor office has a bell on the door and a coffee pot that is never quite empty.

places.name: Lakefront Park
places.description: A strip of beach, lawn and picnic tables beside the marina. The pavilion hosts the weekly farmers' market in summer and Harbor Fest in September.

places.name: Alder Market
places.description: The town's only full grocery store, with a deli counter, a rack of local apples and a bulletin board covered in lost-cat flyers. By the entrance, a Lakeshore Credit Union counter and an ATM that takes deposits.

places.name: Shoreline Fuel
places.description: A gas station and convenience store on the road out of town, with four pumps, a car wash and surprisingly good hot dogs.

places.name: Shoreline Dunes Trail System
places.description: Twelve miles of marked sand trails through the dunes, open to ATVs and side-by-sides from a trailhead lot off County Road 12. The sand is deep, the views are huge and the rules are posted on a sign no one reads.

places.name: Gull Island State Park
places.description: A wooded island six kilometers offshore with a lighthouse, a small campground and a ferry that runs from the marina several times a day in season.

places.name: Chicago, Illinois
places.description: The nearest big city, about a three-and-a-half-hour drive around the bottom of the lake, in the Central time zone: an hour behind Port Alder.

places.name: Lakeshore Consolidated School
places.description: A low brick school on the edge of town that serves Port Alder and the farms behind the dunes: one long corridor, a gym that doubles as the auditorium, and a flagpole in front. Classes run from eight until ten past three.

places.name: 12 Birch Lane
places.description: Marcus Delgado's two-storey clapboard house on a quiet lane above the harbor, with a detached garage he never parks in.

characters.name: Jordan Ellis
characters.summary: Eight months into the job and a year into living in Port Alder, you are good with engines, careful with money and still learning the town's unwritten rules. You rent 2B above the hardware store, make payments on a pickup older than it looks, and keep an old fishing boat on a trailer at the marina for days off.

characters.name: Marcus Delgado
characters.summary: Heavy-set, patient and fond of old pickup trucks. He built the shop up over eleven years, remembers every customer's name and keeps a lot of his worries to himself.

schedule.activity: running the counter and the books
running the counter and the books

characters.name: Danny Okafor
characters.summary: Funny, quick with a wrench and a little too keen on being the one who knows how to fix things. He has worked at the shop six years and lives in 2A, across the landing from you.

characters.name: Priya Nair
characters.role: Township accountant and Harbor Fest organizer
characters.summary: Organized, warm and permanently carrying a clipboard. She keeps the township's books, runs the festival committee and is quietly hoping someone will volunteer to help.

characters.name: Jess Kowalczyk
characters.summary: Dry-witted, sharp with names and pouring a pint faster than anyone in town. She lives in 1A with her grandmother and her fifteen-year-old sister, Maddie, and is saving to start a boat-charter business of her own.

goals.label: Save for a charter boat
steps: Look at three boats for sale
Draft a business plan and show it to Dale

characters.name: Maddie Kowalczyk
characters.summary: Fifteen, quick and a little too observant, Jess's kid sister is a sophomore at Lakeshore Consolidated. She lives in 1A with Jess and their grandmother, rides to school on the morning bus, and spends her free hours at the coffee shop or hanging around the marina dock.

characters.name: Dale Whitcomb
characters.summary: Weathered, deliberate and usually wearing a faded cap from a long-closed tackle shop. He has run the marina for twenty-five years and is happiest when someone asks him how to read the lake.

characters.name: Helen Kowalczyk
characters.role: Landlady and owner of 114 Harbor Street
characters.summary: Small, firm and fond of crossword puzzles and the ball game on the radio. She has owned the building for forty years, keeps the rents low and knows every tenant's footsteps on the stairs.

goals.label: Keep the building in good repair
steps: Plan the winter heating with the plumber

characters.name: Nora Whitfield
characters.role: Registered nurse at the Community Clinic
characters.summary: Tired, funny and endlessly practical. She works three twelve-hour shifts a week, lives alone with a very old cat, and would like very much to sleep through one entire Saturday.

characters.name: Sam Reyes
characters.summary: Calm, dry and good at finding the lost dog in under an hour. Sam works the afternoon shift and knows who is parked where in this town.

goals.label: Keep Harbor Fest orderly
steps: Plan the traffic cones with Priya
Be at the parade route by 14:00 on Saturday

truth.truth: Alder Automotive is about $112,000 behind on its lease and its lift-equipment loan after a slow winter. He wants the township contract to prove the shop can pay its own way.

climates.label: Continental big-city lakefront

lore.title: Port Alder
lore.text: Port Alder sits on the east shore of Lake Michigan with about 6,500 residents. It began as a lumber port, became a fruit-shipping town and is now mostly a place where people fish, sail, ride dune buggies and commute to somewhere larger. It has two stoplights, one high school and no tolerance for being called quaint.

lore.title: 114 Harbor Street
lore.text: 114 Harbor Street is a brick building with Harbor Hardware on the ground floor and four apartments above. Helen Kowalczyk has owned it for forty years and keeps the rents under what the neighbors charge. The stairs creak on the ninth step, and everyone on the second floor knows who is coming home.

lore.title: Alder Automotive
lore.text: Alder Automotive has three bays, a counter, a parts shelf and a back lot of cars waiting for a part. Marcus Delgado opened it eleven years ago. It repairs everything from boat trailers to the township's tractors and is the first place locals call when a tow is needed.

lore.title: The Rusty Anchor
lore.text: The Rusty Anchor is the local bar and grill. It has a deck over the harbor, a wall of old buoys, a pool table with a wobbly leg and a Thursday trivia night that gets competitive. The burger is excellent. The jukebox only plays a handful of songs, and everyone knows them all.

lore.title: Bluebird Coffee
lore.text: Bluebird Coffee is a bright corner cafe on Main Street with a good espresso machine, an overworked barista and a pastry case that empties by ten. A drip coffee costs three dollars; a latte costs about six. Half the town's business is conducted at its mismatched tables.

lore.title: Alder Township Hall
lore.text: The township handles permits, property taxes, the vehicle yard and the festival fund. Its staff is small and overworked: an accountant, a clerk, a supervisor and a handful of part-timers. It owns a fleet of aging trucks that are serviced wherever the lowest bidder is this year.

lore.title: Alder Community Clinic
lore.text: A one-storey clinic with urgent care, primary care and a pharmacy window. It covers most of what a small town needs, and sends the rest to a hospital forty minutes away. Staff are friendly, the waiting room is cold, and the vending machine is always out of the good snack.

lore.title: Alder Harbor Marina
lore.text: The marina has eighty slips, a boat ramp, a fuel dock and a barn for winter storage. Dale Whitcomb has run it for twenty-five years. In season, a slip rents by the month; for guests, a night at the dock is cheap and the coffee in the office is free. Dale lets a few regulars keep a trailered boat in the yard by the ramp, and launches it for them on request.

lore.title: Lakefront Park
lore.text: A strip of beach, lawn and picnic tables beside the marina, with a pavilion that hosts the farmers' market on summer Saturdays. It fills up on the Fourth of July and on the fourth weekend of September for Harbor Fest.

lore.title: Alder Market
lore.text: The only full grocery store in town carries what you need, a few things you don't and a rack of local apples in fall. Its bulletin board advertises everything from lost cats to dune-buggy repairs. Prices run a little under national averages.

lore.title: Shoreline Fuel
lore.text: Shoreline Fuel has four pumps, a car wash and a rotating selection of hot dogs. Regular gasoline runs about three dollars and fifteen cents a gallon. It is open from five in the morning until eleven at night and is the first place anyone stops after a flat tire.

lore.title: Shoreline Dunes Trail System
lore.text: Twelve miles of marked sand trails run through the dunes, open to ATVs and side-by-sides from a trailhead off County Road 12. Riders must stay on the marked trail, wear helmets, and keep an eye on the weather: a front can roll off the lake in minutes.

lore.title: Gull Island State Park
lore.text: Gull Island has a lighthouse, a small campground and a long shingle beach. A ferry from the marina makes the crossing in about twenty-five minutes, several times a day in season, and costs around nine dollars. It does not run when the wind is up.

lore.title: Harbor Fest
lore.text: Harbor Fest is held on the fourth Saturday of September. It has food stalls, a brass band, a pie contest and a parade of decorated boats at two in the afternoon. The township's festival fund pays for most of it, and Priya Nair has organized it for the last four years.

lore.title: Marcus Delgado
lore.text: Marcus Delgado owns Alder Automotive. He is fifty-two, heavy-set and patient, and fixes everything slowly and well. Employees say he never raises his voice and never forgets a mistake. He works longer hours than any of them.

lore.title: Danny Okafor
lore.text: Danny Okafor is the shop's senior mechanic. Thirty-one, funny and fast, he knows every engine in town by its sound. He lives in 2A and tells everyone he has no plans to leave Port Alder, though he drives down to Chicago to see his family when the shop can spare him. He is competitive in a way he thinks is invisible.

lore.title: Priya Nair
lore.text: Priya Nair is the township accountant and Harbor Fest's organizer. She is warm, brisk and permanently holding a clipboard. She can tell you the festival budget to the dollar and the name of every vendor's cousin.

lore.title: Jess Kowalczyk
lore.text: Jess Kowalczyk tends bar at the Rusty Anchor five nights a week. Twenty-four, dry-witted and exact with a pour, she lives in 1A with her grandmother and her kid sister Maddie, and spends her days off looking at boats she cannot yet afford.

lore.title: Maddie Kowalczyk
lore.text: Maddie Kowalczyk is fifteen, Jess's kid sister, and a sophomore at Lakeshore Consolidated. She walks to the bus on school mornings, does her homework at the Bluebird Coffee shop twice a week and spends Friday afternoons on the marina dock, where Dale lets her coil lines in return for a lesson now and then.

lore.title: Lakeshore Consolidated School
lore.text: Lakeshore Consolidated serves Port Alder and the farms behind the dunes. The fall term began on Monday 31 August and runs to Friday 20 November; the school closes for Thanksgiving week, reopens on Monday 30 November and lets out for winter break after Friday 18 December. Classes run from eight o'clock until ten past three.

lore.title: Dale Whitcomb
lore.text: Dale Whitcomb owns the marina. Sixty-one, weathered and unhurried, he is happiest when someone asks him how to read the lake. He lends boats to people he trusts, and has strong opinions about the people he does not.

lore.title: Helen Kowalczyk
lore.text: Helen Kowalczyk, seventy-one, owns 114 Harbor Street and has lived on its ground floor for forty years. She is firm, kind, nosy in equal measure, and still does the crossword in pen.

lore.title: Nora Whitfield
lore.text: Nora Whitfield is a nurse at the clinic. She works three twelve-hour shifts a week, lives alone with an elderly cat, and is the person to ask about any medical question at three in the morning.

lore.title: Sam Reyes
lore.text: Officer Sam Reyes works the afternoon patrol. Calm and dry, Sam is more likely to resolve a dispute with a conversation than a ticket, and has found the missing dog in less than an hour more times than anyone can count.

lore.title: The lake
lore.text: Lake Michigan is calm for weeks and then, with almost no warning, isn't. Locals check the marine forecast before they put a boat in the water, and the marina flies a pennant when a small-craft advisory is in force.

lore.title: Living in Port Alder
lore.text: Port Alder is cheaper than most of the country: a one-bedroom rents for about eleven hundred dollars a month, groceries cost a little under the national average and electricity runs close to twenty cents a kilowatt-hour. A mechanic makes about twenty-four dollars an hour and a nurse about forty-five.

args.text: Marcus slides the township pickup's work order across the counter: it cranks and does not catch, and the contract depends on it.

args.text: The old relay clicks and does nothing; the spare from the RELAYS bin fits, and the pickup catches on the first try.
